engine: Compass judge (impact, moat, quality and ORION's dimensions; Jev beliefs over described situations) · ORION prioritisation (Borda over RICE, ICE, WSJF, leverage, Eisenhower) · ORION aftermath

criteria.rule: High value: impact score at least 2.5 of 4 (halfway from "noticeably" to "substantially" moves the most important goal).
criteria.verdicts: high value = meets the rule · kept as a prerequisite = below the rule, but a high-value item cannot run without it · cut = below the rule and nothing high-value needs it · rejected on evidence = tried and measured worse or unidentified.

note: The scores are a model's judgment of the descriptions and evidence shown here; the verdict is the fixed rule applied to them.

items.title: Checked against real F-106B flight and trim data
items.detail: Elevon lift and trim from the same lattice, a rounded-leading-edge blend, and a comparison with NASA's published F-106B trim table (absolute) and 27 flight points (shape), scored leave-one-flight-out.

evidence.line: Lift error at NASA's trim point 63% before, 3% after; elevon within 0.469°; held-out weight spread 6% (target 5%).

items.title: F-16 flown on NASA's measured whole-aircraft data
items.detail: Rigid-body pitch dynamics on NASA's measured forces and pitching moment (TP-1538 Table III, 20 angles of attack by 5 stabilator settings, flap and pitch-rate terms), published mass and pitch inertia, NASA's stabilator and leading-edge-flap actuators and schedule, NASA's thrust table; the stick drives the stabilator through a stated control law. Replaces the drag allowance and the stick-sets-α shortcut.

items.title: Unaugmented mode and hard physical limits
items.detail: A mode with no flight-control system (the stick positions the stabilator; the airframe is unstable at this centre of gravity), live modes of motion from the linearised equations, NASA's pilot blackout rule, the USAF 9 g limit and a hard stop at Mach 0.6 where NASA's data end.
items.ownerRequest: 2026-11-23: physics as close to reality as possible, harsher if needed, with different modes

evidence.line: The flap schedule turns a pitch divergence doubling every 1.2 s (flap frozen) into one doubling every 11 s at 500 ft/s, and makes the 300 ft/s case stable: the readout shows both. Blackout times match NASA's rule exactly; Whinnery & Forster's 888 centrifuge cases (mean 9.1 s, never under 5 s) agree in size.
